claims.text: The initial material is single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a single-phase fcc FeCoNi-derived high-entropy alloy.
Thermal annealing can induce precipitation of a Co-rich secondary phase in the specified FeCoNi-based alloys.
Annealing at 500–700 °C for 1–10 hours is an appropriate processing window for producing the proposed precipitates.
The precipitated Co-rich phase has a high magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant.
A secondary phase having high magnetocrystalline anisotropy can act as a domain-wall-pinning population.
Domain-wall pinning increases the energy required for domain-wall motion.
Increased resistance to domain-wall motion increases coercive field.
Introducing a second phase can be associated with increased coercivity in a high-entropy alloy.
The intervention will increase coercive field by at least a factor of five relative to the single-phase fcc FeCoNi material or matched derivative.
The applicable baseline alloys have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
The compositional scope is limited to FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys whose compositions deviate by no more than 10% from equiatomic FeCoNi.
After intervention, the material retains an fcc matrix or structure while containing a thermally precipitated secondary phase.
The predicted coercivity change applies to magnetic measurements performed at room temperature.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on annealing conditions, composition, and microstructure.
